claims.text: An integrated HT-XRD and TGA setup can concurrently measure oxidation kinetics through mass change and phase transformations during high-temperature oxidation.
The CrCoFeMnNi starting alloy is equiatomic.
The starting alloy is homogenized, single-phase, and a uniform solid solution produced by arc melting and annealing.
Simultaneous in situ HT-XRD and TGA can be performed during an oxidation test.
The relevant oxidation environment is above 800°C.
Precisely controlled oxygen partial pressures can mimic realistic service conditions.
TGA mass-change measurements can serve as an indicator of oxidation kinetics.
In situ HT-XRD tracks crystal-structure and phase evolution during high-temperature oxidation.
Real-time correlation of oxidation-related mass changes with concurrent phase transformations provides a dynamic understanding of oxidation.
In situ measurement can capture time-temperature-dependent oxide formation and phase transformations.
Integrating HT-XRD and TGA captures oxidation and phase evolution in a single experimental run.
The integrated method overcomes limitations of ex situ or disconnected analyses.
The method will reveal a direct correlation between mass gain or loss and the onset of phase changes.
Integrated HT-XRD and TGA will depict oxidation behavior and phase stability more accurately than separate TGA or ex situ XRD.
Standalone TGA or post-mortem XRD cannot resolve the real-time interplay between oxidation kinetics and phase transitions.
The approach is limited to temperatures typically above 800°C.
Instrument response time may limit detection of rapid transient phenomena.
The quantitative relationship between mass change and phase evolution may vary with alloy composition and experimental conditions.
Synchronization and resolution limitations may make an integrated instrument perform worse than separately optimized instruments.
